newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks hit hard by Brazilian "samba effect".
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks hit hard by Brazilian "samba effect".

text.p: Mexican stocks fell sharply Tuesday, dragged lower by profit-taking and a steep drop in the stock market in Brazil.
"The 'samba effect' from Brazil has hit all Latam markets today. The market is worried over pressure to devalue in Brazil," one trader said.
Mexico's IPC share index tumbled 82.72 points or 1.73 percent to 4,694.35.
In Sao Paulo, the Bovespa index of most active stocks plunged 1,081 points, or 8.5 percent, to 11,617.
Analysts said Mexican shares had fallen in part because dealers have been taking profits since Friday, after eight consecutive record highs.

"The adjustment under way since Friday was almost inevitable, and was exacerbated by the falls in Brazil, but we have stood up well compared to other Latin American markets," said Felix Boni, head of research at ING-Barings in Mexico.
The Argentine Merval blue-chip index fell 3.37 percent to 807.91, while the IPSA selective index in Chile was down 2.57 percent at 131.25 points.
Grey Newman, James Capel's chief economist for Mexico, said there were limits to the ills affecting the Brazilian stock market since Mexico did not have a burgeoning trade deficit like Brazil's.

"Mexico's economy has some good news in store," he said. "We predict the economy will grow by 5.5 percent in the second quarter, and there should be some feeding through in corporate earnings in the coming weeks."
Newman said he expected domestic unemployment and retail sales data due later in the week to reinforce the perception of an improving Mexican economy.
Dealers said trading volume of 93.2 million shares was more moderate than many sessions last week, suggesting that investors had not yet jumped out of Mexico.

Market heavyweight Telmex (Telefonos de Mexico) fell 50 centavos (6 cents) to 20.30 pesos ($2.56). Similarly, the telecom company's ADRs dropped to 49-3/4 in late trade before recovering a bit to end down 2-3/16 at 50-13/16.
Dealers said the decline on the Brazilian market overshadowed gains on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones industrial average rose 52.73 points to 7,975.71, a record, and within 25 points of 8,000.
In the broader market in Mexico, declining issues outnumbered gainers 85 to 16.
